framework_notes: Flask is the primary web framework (score 1.00 >= 0.75 threshold); references/flask.md was loaded in addition to references/python.md and references/patterns.md.

Routes are registered via blueprint decorators `@<bp>.route(...)` on module-level functions (no handler classes), so source extraction keys on decorator-detected handler functions and their parameters, plus `request.*` accessor shapes from references/flask.md section 6.
The Kobo blueprint mounts at /kobo/<auth_token>, so part of the URL path is both an auth token and request-derived input; kobo_auth.register_url_value_preprocessor (cps/kobo.py:62) preprocesses it.

Flask-Login wraps most user-facing routes with @login_required variants; admin routes add @admin_required; upload-dependent branches check current_user.role_upload() at runtime (cps/editbooks.py:802).

notes: Extraction rules were derived only from repository evidence and the CWE-918 pass focus; no vulnerability ground truth, CVE descriptions, fix diffs, or pre-located vulnerable lines were consulted.

Both extraction queries are plain multi-column select queries (no @kind metadata) for use with `codeql query run` + `codeql bqrs decode`; they are not intended for `codeql database analyze` SARIF output.
CSV column order matches the prior-project convention: node, candidate_type, callable, flow_kind, receiver, moduleHint, arg_index, line, file:line, expression. arg_index is -1 when not applicable.

flow_kind vocabulary: param/return/field/argument as in prior projects, plus 'call' for wrapper-invocation sink candidates whose URL is constructed inside the wrapper (documented in sinks.ql comments).

AST-literal matching (e.g. requests.get by object Name 'requests') is used because CodeQL resolved-API modeling is not guaranteed for the optional dependencies of this project; import resolution must be validated during LLM labeling (all matched call sites were individually confirmed against the source).
urllib.request.urlopen / urlretrieve / httpx are NOT used anywhere in this source tree (verified by grep) - no candidates and no coverage gap for those APIs.
file:/data: schemes and other non-HTTP(S) loaders: no code path in this project constructs such URLs for network loading; nothing extracted.

coverage_gaps: cps/services/gmail.py: google-api-client network calls (setup_gmail lines ~52/57, get_user_info ~71, send_messsage ~85-94: creds.refresh(Request()), build(serviceName=...), service.users().messages().send(...).execute()) issue real HTTP to fixed Google endpoints with admin-configured credentials; no user-controllable URL argument is provable from this source, so they are not extracted as sink candidates. If labeling later treats OAuth token refresh as in-scope, these must be added manually.
cps/services/goodreads_support.py: GoodreadsClient(key, secret) wrapper - network I/O happens inside the goodreads/betterreads library with admin-configured API keys; not extracted.
cps/oauth_bb.py + flask_dance OAuth blueprints (GitHub/Google, cps/oauth_bb.py:249): provider endpoints fixed by blueprint configuration; token exchange happens inside flask_dance; not extracted.

cps/metadata_provider/scholar.py: the actual HTTP requests for scholarly.search_pubs happen inside the scholarly package, which is not part of this CodeQL database; only the wrapper call site is extracted, so intra-library flows are invisible to taint tracking.

cps/updater.py parent_commit['url'] (line 352): URL values echoed from earlier GitHub API JSON responses are second-order network-derived input; extracted as a requests.get sink, but the response-to-URL propagation would need a summary step in Phase 2 if labeling considers it in-scope.
CPS helpers that only parse URLs (urlparse in cps/helper.py:736, urljoin not used) are intentionally not sinks; only actual network I/O call sites are extracted.
